Definition: Whether consumer protection legislation or regulations specifically address digital payment services, covering disclosure requirements, liability allocation for unauthorized transactions, error resolution procedures, and user rights.
Comments: Angola enacted a comprehensive Consumer Protection Law — Law No. 15/03 of 22 July 2003 (Lei de Defesa do Consumidor). This law establishes consumer rights including quality of goods and services, economic protection, right to information, and redress mechanisms. It covers financial services and electronic payments. The law establishes administrative sanctions including fines, suspension of services, and other remedies. This is a full consumer protection legal framework applicable to payment services.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The originally cited source (general Consumer Protection Law 15/03, 2003) alone would only support 'Partial' per the metadata definition, since it is not payment-specific. However, corroborating research found BNA Aviso n.12/2016 (Proteção dos Consumidores de Produtos e Serviços Financeiros), a dedicated financial-consumer-protection instrument mandating complaint-handling units, 20-day resolution timelines and escalation to BNA, and payment-specific Avisos (07/2017 Art.29-30; 05/2017 Art.12; 05/22 Ch. IX 'Protecção ao Utilizador e Resolução de Disputas') that explicitly extend and apply these consumer-protection rules to payment service providers, plus dedicated dispute-resolution and call-centre obligations. This combination constitutes a comprehensive, payment-specific consumer protection framework, so Value Code 3 (Yes) is confirmed, though on stronger grounds than the original single source provided.

Definition: Whether payment system operators or regulators regularly publish performance metrics and statistics on system usage, transaction volumes/values, participant numbers, uptime, and other operational indicators.
Comments: EMIS publishes an annual Relatório & Contas (Annual Report and Accounts) which includes operational payment statistics. BNA also provides annual data through its payment system oversight function and publishes quarterly financial soundness indicators. The EMIS website confirms publication of Relatório & Contas 2024. BNA disclosed 2025 operational payment statistics through CCENIF sessions. Reporting is primarily annual; some operational data is shared more frequently in press releases. No evidence of systematic monthly/quarterly public performance reports for the payment system.

revision_notes: Verified that MULTICAIXA/EMIS operates a public statistics portal (multicaixa.ao/indicadores) presenting 'evolução mensal' (monthly evolution) of TPA/ATM terminal counts, transaction volumes and values by channel and card numbers, in addition to EMIS's annual Relatório & Contas (2024/2025) and BNA's periodic disclosures (e.g. Nov 2025 data presented Dec 2025, full-year 2025 results announced Jan 2026). This meets the 'Monthly/Quarterly' public-reporting threshold rather than merely 'Annual', so Value Code is raised from 3 to 4.
